resources.string: Stops the active band alarm when tap response is enabled in Alarms.
Logs your configured amount inside its confirmation window.
Runs the general double-tap action selected above.
When Safety is ready, the required repeated double-taps take priority, immediately page accepted contacts, and start current-location sharing when available.

Encrypted exports protect database history and durable settings with AES-256-GCM. NOOP never saves or recovers the passphrase. Credentials, hardware links, permissions, and temporary delivery state are excluded. New backups include an integrity manifest; legacy unencrypted backups still import. Restore validates and stages data before reopening the database. Cross-platform export moves supported data between Apple and Android. Folder and automatic backups are unencrypted, so use encrypted storage.

Export data creates a portable ZIP with compatible CSVs, readable NOOP JSON for editable nutrition and Strength Trainer records, and a comparison folder with source-separated daily metrics, sleep, workouts, and metric series. Keep the original provider ZIP unchanged and separate for side-by-side analysis.
Saved %1$s. The ZIP re-imports into NOOP on Mac, iPhone, or Android. Its comparison folder is ready for side-by-side analysis; keep the original provider ZIP unchanged and share both files together.
Active energy comes from the phone health store. Noop Band\'s combined HR-based calorie estimate is a different quantity and is not mixed into this calendar.
Each square is one day: red is a low day, amber middling, mint strong. An empty outline means no data; gaps stay gaps.
Load is an experimental estimate from resting heart rate and HRV only, not a scored metric. Treat it as a hint.
Nutrition shows calories you logged. A blank day means not logged, never zero intake.
Imported daily stress is used when available. Other days require a reliable two-signal experimental autonomic estimate from resting heart rate and HRV; limited estimates stay blank.
Days without data are left empty; they are not counted as zero.
Wear Noop Band overnight to build skin-temperature and body-clock observations.
Cycle day is anchored to your logged start. The broad period window uses a 28-day prior while nightly temperature calibration continues.
The estimated window from your last log has passed. Log the next start when it happens; NOOP will not roll an old date forward.
Learning your pattern from your nightly temperature - keep wearing it overnight.
Your temperature shift came at a different time than your logged date - the logged start may be off.
No clear temperature pattern yet - this can happen with irregular cycles, hormonal birth control, or shift work.
Cycle day is anchored to your latest start. The period window uses your recent logged intervals and expands with their variability.
Follicular range - temperature sitting at your baseline.
Luteal range - temperature is running above your baseline.
Around your mid-cycle shift - temperature is turning.
Your last logged start is over 40 days old. Log the latest start to refresh this estimate; NOOP will not roll an old date forward.
Log a period start and wear Noop Band overnight to begin a private estimate.
Turn on cycle awareness to read a coarse phase from your nightly temperature.
Recent logged cycle lengths vary too much or include an interval outside the supported range for a useful period forecast. Cycle day still counts from your latest start.
Likely period window: %1$s to %2$s. This is a range, not a fixed date.
Menstrual cycle, %1$s. Opens private period, flow and symptom tracking.
Private period, flow and symptom tracking

In Noop, open More → Friends and enter the server address and one-time code.
Values retain their original source and recorded date. Sparklines appear only for recent, closely spaced observations; missing periods are not connected. These are not diagnoses or targets.
Add an optional target in Profile.
Whole-body values retain their recorded source. NOOP does not infer arm, leg, or trunk fat and muscle distribution; that requires compatible segmental measurement hardware.

Rename, regroup, or remove an item to tidy your list. Renaming keeps the original question behind the scenes, so imported references still line up. Custom items are deleted; built-in ones are hidden and can be restored below.
Project terms and source license. Available offline.

The first minute stays quiet. Then 2 light taps mean increase effort after 25 seconds below target; 3 firm taps mean ease off after a sharp rise stays above target for 25 seconds. Brief spikes stay silent, and the same cue waits at least 50 seconds.
Know what will happen before the session starts. Nothing is tracked until you tap Start coaching.
End the session at any time. Missing heart-rate data pauses cues after about 8 seconds and automatically ends the session after 10 minutes without a reading.
Today\'s Recovery, your recent resting heart rate, and profile max heart rate set the range. Without a Recovery score, NOOP uses a cautious middle range.
Live heart-rate trends and time inside, below, and above today\'s target band. This coaching session does not create a workout entry.
Start workout coach. Beta. Band vibrations guide effort using today\'s Recovery and heart rate.
Band vibrations guide effort using today\'s Recovery and heart rate.
Check the original source and measurement method. Confirm an unexpected value with an appropriate thermometer and seek care when symptoms warrant it.
Measurement site, device, timing and environment vary. This is not core-temperature monitoring or a diagnosis.
NOOP preserves the source value in its own series and does not substitute it for skin-temperature deviation.
Body or basal-body temperature is an absolute temperature reading imported from Health Connect.
Repeated readings from the same method can add context to how you feel and to cycle-aware patterns.
Open the heart-rate trace with workout context. Check band fit when values look implausible and compare similar activities.
Sampling gaps and optical artifacts can miss peaks or bias an average. A high value during exercise is not, by itself, a rhythm finding.
Calculated by the identified source from its available heart-rate samples and imported without filling gaps.
This chart shows the source\'s daily average or maximum heart rate, as named above.
With activity context, it helps explain cardiovascular demand and whether the source captured the day.
Inspect the sleep timeline for long awake periods. Keep wake time consistent for several nights and discuss persistent sleep concerns with a clinician.
Quiet wakefulness can be classified as sleep. This is a wearable estimate, not a clinical sleep measure.
Calculated as detected asleep time divided by time in bed and displayed as a percentage.
Sleep efficiency is the share of your in-bed window that NOOP classified as asleep.
It helps distinguish too little sleep opportunity from a fragmented or wakeful sleep window.
Compare similar activities and check workout type, duration and the heart-rate trace. Check band fit when the trace looks implausible.
Heart-rate load does not fully capture muscular, technical or emotional difficulty. Optical sensors can miss short spikes.
Computed on device from time and intensity across your heart-rate zones. The same stored score can appear on a 0 to 100 or 0 to 21 scale.
Effort is NOOP\'s cardiovascular-load score for the day.
It helps compare the internal load of different workouts and active days.
Follow the trend from a consistent source. Check related metrics and how you feel, and confirm implausible readings before acting on them.
Source algorithms and coverage differ. One value is not a diagnosis or a complete picture of your health.
Measured, imported or derived by the source attached to each reading. NOOP does not invent missing values.
This is a metric in your NOOP timeline. Its exact meaning depends on the identified source.
Its trend can add context when compared with your own history and related signals.
Compare like-for-like overnight readings. Consider an easier load when HRV and other recovery signals shift together and you also feel run down.
HRV differs greatly between people. Rhythm artifacts, short samples and timing can change it, so compare with your own trend.
Derived from clean beat-to-beat intervals and stored as RMSSD in milliseconds. Dense overnight data is preferred; imported readings remain identified.
Heart-rate variability, or HRV, is the variation in time between consecutive heart beats.
Compared with your personal baseline, overnight HRV can show shifts in autonomic recovery and accumulated stress.
Log at a consistent time and add journal context for unusual days. Seek qualified support for persistent distress or safety concerns.
A simple check-in is not a mental-health screening or diagnosis.
Stored exactly as you log it and kept on device unless you choose to share it.
Mood is your own non-clinical daily check-in.
It keeps subjective experience beside physiology instead of assuming sensors know how you feel.
Log consistently before comparing trends. Use multi-day patterns and consult a qualified professional for individualized nutrition care.
Portion estimates, database errors and incomplete logging can outweigh small day-to-day differences.
Manual entries and imported daily summaries are added as entered. Missing nutrients stay missing, not zero.
This chart shows the selected calorie or macronutrient total from meals you logged or imported.
Consistent intake logs can be compared with training, sleep and recovery patterns.
Use the score with how you feel. Prioritize sleep, food and fluids, and ease load when several recovery signals shift together.
Recovery is a wellness estimate, not a health measurement or permission to train.
Computed on device from HRV against your baseline, resting heart rate, sleep, breathing rate, skin temperature deviation and recent load when available.
Recovery is NOOP\'s 0 to 100 estimate of how ready your body appears for load today.
It combines several overnight recovery trends into one planning signal.
Recheck across another night when you feel well. Look for matching HRV, resting-heart-rate or temperature shifts and seek medical advice for persistent changes or breathing symptoms.
Movement, fit and source algorithms affect the value. It is not a lung-function test.
Estimated from the selected wearable or an overnight signal and compared with your personal history.
Respiratory rate is the estimated number of breaths per minute during rest or sleep.
It is usually steady for one person, so a sustained shift can be a useful context signal.
Compare several similar nights instead of one point. Check sleep, recent load, fluids and how you feel when it rises with other signals.
Medication, posture, sensor fit and measurement timing can shift the number. One reading is rarely meaningful alone.
Taken from the most stable available low-activity or sleep period in the selected day\'s resolved data.
Resting heart rate is your heart rate during a low-activity or sleep period.
A sustained change from your own baseline can reflect shifts in recovery, fitness, stress or environment.
NOOP cannot diagnose a condition. If a change persists, worsens, or comes with symptoms, speak with a qualified clinician. Seek urgent care for urgent symptoms.
Protect enough time in bed for your current sleep need. Keep wake time reasonably consistent for several nights and inspect the sleep timeline when a total looks wrong.
Wearables estimate sleep and stages. They are not clinical sleep tests and can mistake quiet wakefulness for sleep.
Calculated from the detected sleep window minus detected awake time. Imported sleep data remains identified separately from NOOP detection.
Sleep duration is the estimated time you were asleep within a detected sleep window.
Sleep quantity and timing can affect recovery, attention, mood and training response.
Repeat an unexpected reading with warm skin and a secure fit. Confirm concerning values with a validated device and seek medical advice for repeated low confirmed readings or symptoms.
Cold skin, motion, fit, skin characteristics and device quality can distort wrist readings. NOOP is not a pulse oximeter or medical device.
Measured by a compatible optical sensor or imported from a connected source. NOOP preserves the source instead of treating every device as equivalent.
Blood oxygen, or SpO₂, estimates the percentage of hemoglobin carrying oxygen.
Repeated, trustworthy measurements can add context about overnight oxygenation and altitude response.
Allow notifications in Settings to receive the optional Effort marker. NOOP still works normally without it.
The Lock Screen only says the recap is ready. Recovery and Sleep Score values stay inside NOOP.
Notifications are disabled in system settings.
Available measured signals are close to your recent baseline.
A current daily row and enough prior nights are needed for this read.
A few more nights of data and your readiness read will sharpen.
Supporting prior days: %1$d. The personal baseline is still building.
No current recovery signal has enough prior variation for comparison.
No daily recovery row is available for this date.
This read is based on one current recovery signal.
Your measured recovery trends are aligned with your recent baseline.
Several measured signals shifted from your recent range. Recheck the trend and use how you feel as context.
One measured signal shifted from your recent range. A single day is a cue to recheck, not a diagnosis or training instruction.

NOOP reads only quiet overnight windows outside recorded workouts. Movement, exercise, elevated non-resting heart rate, and noisy windows are skipped rather than interpreted. It draws the timing between heartbeats as a Poincaré scatter and computes published descriptive statistics. Rhythm is an opt-in picture of timing, never a diagnosis, and it never sends alerts.
This night changed before the edit could be saved. Latest data restored.
Recent balance adds %1$s tonight. This is capped at 1 hour and will never reduce your target.
No recovery time is added tonight. NOOP never recommends less than your target because of a recent surplus.
The plan stays available with reminders off. Turn on the nudge below if you want a gentle notification.
Reminder scheduled for %1$s; delivery is a gentle notification, not a guaranteed alarm.
These are direct log records. NOOP does not infer a one-rep max, muscular strain, or automatic reps from them.
Factual records from completed manual sets.
Primary muscles receive full set credit; supporting muscles receive half. This maps your log, not physiological muscle load.
No muscle exposure logged this week
Optional detail-free breathing prompts after a qualified resting signal.
Requires fresh R-R timing, fresh heart rate, a worn encrypted band, and dense timestamp-matched wrist motion. Missing or moving data never triggers a suggestion.
Opt in to private breathing suggestions based on your own resting heart-timing baseline. This is a wellness signal, not a stress diagnosis.
Manual Breathe remains available from Today’s + menu and More. Automatic checks never poll sensors more often; they evaluate fresh data already received during normal sync.
A fresh wrist signal suggests a short breathing check-in may be useful. Open NOOP when you are ready.
Notifications are disabled in system settings. Enable them there to receive phone prompts.
Also sends one detail-free phone prompt when a qualified check-in appears. Off by default and rate-limited.
Suppress automatic check-ins from 10 PM to 7 AM. Manual Breathe stays available.
Wrist alerts are off. The in-app check-in and an enabled phone prompt still work, but the band will not buzz.
I understand NOOP Band is not available yet. This version currently works with a compatible band I own, and I will use only my own band and my own data.
I understand NOOP is early-access wellness software, provided "as is", and is not a medical device or medical advice.
I have read and accept the full Terms of Use, including the warranty and liability limits allowed by law.
NOOP is developed independently. Current direct-band support is provided for compatibility testing while NOOP Band is in development.
This build is provided "as is" while NOOP Band and its software are in development. Read the full terms for warranty and liability limits.
NOOP\'s metrics are wellness estimates. Do not use them to diagnose, treat, or make medical or emergency decisions. Seek qualified care when needed.
Connect only a band you own and use NOOP only with your own data. Direct compatibility may affect another app\'s connection, account services, device support, or warranty.
Until NOOP Band is ready, this version works with a compatible band you own.
